title: PROFUZZ: Directed Graybox Fuzzing via Module Selection and ATPG-Guided Seed Generation
problem: Directed hardware fuzzing struggles with precise seed generation for specific submodules, suffering from limited HDL support, abstraction mismatches, and poor scalability for large designs.
motivation: Scalable, precise seed generation is critical for efficiently testing large-scale hardware designs with coverage-guided fuzzing.
method: PROFUZZ combines two techniques: automatic structural analysis of hardware (ATPG) and directed graybox fuzzing (testing that targets specific hardware parts using partial knowledge of their design). Rather than creating random starting test cases, PROFUZZ leverages ATPG's understanding of hardware structure to generate smarter seeds for each module. This approach enables precise testing of specific hardware components and better scalability for large designs.
key_novelty: The core idea is using ATPG (automatic structural analysis of hardware) to generate smarter starting test cases for directed fuzzing of specific modules.
contributions: Integration of ATPG with directed graybox fuzzing for precise seed generation
Improved scalability supporting large target regions
30× greater scalability in terms of handling target sites
11.66% higher coverage with 2.76× faster execution vs DirectFuzz
limitations: Evaluation against DirectFuzz only; comparison with other directed fuzzing approaches missing.
primary_theme: ATPG-guided directed fuzzing for hardware verification
